title: Implement message ack isolation and rate-sensitive throttler
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Background: Our async ingestion pipeline uses a mix of Redis streams and Kafka consumers across several tenants. Operational incidents over the last 6 months repeatedly trace back to two interacting problems: (1) ack/commit side effects that are not isolated per ingestion worker shard, causing duplicate message processing and opaque reenqueue behavior under retries; (2) a single global shedder that responds to latency spikes by hard-throttling, which regresses high-priority tenants and causes cascading timeouts.

Goal: Reduce duplicate processing and improve latency SLO adherence by (A) introducing ack isolation (per-shard ack/commit buffers + defensive commit ordering) so retries and out-of-order callbacks cannot ack unrelated messages, and (B) replacing the global shedder with a rate-sensitive throttler that enforces per-tenant rate windows and a cooperative backpressure API for callers.

Scope:
- Redis consumer and Redis-streams-based retry path (primary).
- Kafka consumer connector changes required for commit semantics parity (secondary).
- No protocol changes to customer-facing API; this is internal delivery/infrastructure work.

Design summary:
1) Ack isolation
- Introduce a small per-executor ack buffer keyed by (ingest_shard, partition, message_id) and a deterministic commit sequencer that enforces strict monotonic commit per-partition.
- Move ack/commit responsibilities out of retry handlers into a single committer actor per-shard to avoid races between success, retry, and delayed duplicate callbacks.
- Ensure commits are idempotent: add a lightweight commit token (opaque string) persisted in the in-memory lease and included in the commit call to detect stale ack issuance.

2) Rate-sensitive throttler
- Replace the binary shedder with a token-bucket-based throttler that supports: per-tenant rate budgets, dynamic refill based on observed latency and error budgets, and short-lived burst allowances for high-priority routes.
- Provide a cooperative API: acquireTokens(tenant, cost, deadline) -> tokenGrant | backpressureHint so callers can decide to queue, degrade, or fall back.
- Integrate with the autoscaling signals and routing layer so throttler can temporarily relax rates for tenants pinned to dedicated capacity.

Observability and safety nets:
- Emit metrics: ack_buffer_size, ack_reorder_count, commit_stale_events, throttler_denials_by_tenant, throttler_latency_headroom.
- Introduce a debug mode to snapshot in-flight ack buffers for postmortem.
- End-to-end load test harness: replay recorded production traffic and assert median p99 latencies and dup-processing rate below targets.

Compatibility and rollout strategy:
- Feature-flag both ack isolation and throttler independently per-cluster and per-tenant.
- Canary rollout: enable on non-critical tenants first, run 48h soak with broken-trace comparison; then enable for a subset of critical tenants before platform-wide flip.

Acceptance criteria:
- Duplicate-processing rate (measured as same message reprocessed within 5m window) reduced to <0.01% in load test compared to baseline.
- Peak tail-latency (p99) for ingestion pipelines is no worse than baseline and improves for tenants benefiting from per-tenant rate policies.
- No increase in lost-commit incidents observed in canary; any commit failures must be surfaced to the committer alerting channel and auto-retry within 30s.
- Relevant metrics and dashboards added to Console and included in the rollout runbook.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Full rewrite of Kafka consumer group coordinator behavior; we will mirror commit semantics where feasible but leave deeper Kafka consumer redesign for a follow-up.

Why this differs from prior work:
- Previous tickets focused on coarse-grained backpressure and global retry policies; this ticket combines a correctness-first change (ack isolation) with a more nuanced throttling strategy that preserves per-tenant fairness and priority during load spikes.
